findings.observation: Unconfirmed rollback had no defined knowledge/lifecycle transition or cleanup oracle.
findings.resolution: Closed/InProgress with CommitAttempted=false and RollbackUnconfirmed now distinguishes lack of confirmation from an attempted commit. Earlier Unknown is preserved. DisposeAsync success requires local safety; pending native work retains ownership/budget. TX-V02 explicitly checks these paths.

findings.observation: db-wire/1 did not uniquely locate the cell table.
findings.resolution: Exact checked descriptor/cell/payload formulas define the byte layout; row/count/offset arithmetic, non-overlap, zero-length/null cases, schema/shape and 8-byte table alignment are specified.

findings.observation: Database shutdown wording implied native module unload, conflicting with D02 v1.
findings.resolution: Instance/pool/runtime close is separated from process-lifetime module loading; parent/child leases remain until retire. No hot unload is promised.

findings.observation: DataChangeSet SaveChanges within an outer transaction lacked an acceptance/commit boundary.
findings.resolution: v1 rejects an already Active outer transaction. Rust owns the single transaction and accepts changes only on ConfirmedCommitted; Unknown freezes the change set.

findings.observation: A prebuild extractor cannot demand error-free whole-program binding before its later SG creates façade symbols.
findings.resolution: Pre-extraction validates discovered query/schema declarations and their dependencies. Unrelated execution sites referencing forthcoming generated symbols are left to strict final CoreCompile; genuine declaration errors remain failures.

findings.observation: CloseAsync example used Quarantined as Cleanup.Status although it was absent from that enum.
findings.resolution: Pending is Cleanup.Status; Quarantined is ConnectionDisposition. LocalResourcesReleased=false and retained roots/budget make the finite-wait snapshot distinct from successful disposal.

findings.observation: Generated report URLs treated tag metadata and local experiments as GitHub source paths; R23-C05 displayed the wrong source reader.
findings.resolution: Tag metadata uses its actual API URL. The executed R24 experiment uses a relative script link and exact SHA-256. R23-C05 names /root and R06. Final local-link and invalid-blob-pattern checks pass.

design_conclusions: Rust SeaORM is the actual ORM authority: generated Entity/Model/ActiveModel/Relation/Projection and request lowering execute through SeaORM/SeaQuery/SQLx. C# is syntax/capture/IR/ABI/DTO surface; managed libraries are comparative references only.

A custom SQLx-owning SessionExecutor is a plausible implementation of public SeaORM2.0.4 ConnectionTrait/StreamTrait/TransactionTrait. The associated transaction fixed-point trait is real; private DatabaseTransaction internals are not exposed or relied on. A compiled trait/lifetime/Send fixture is still mandatory in B04/B05.
Commit cancellation is admission-only; after entry, native/domain outcome is preserved, including Unknown. Cleanup and local retire do not establish a remote rollback or commit outcome.

Streams/cursors, transactions and operations hold parent leases and admission/byte budgets. Bounded CloseAsync can report pending without releasing resources; DisposeAsync success requires local safety. SQLite synchronous channel sends and potentially blocking cleanup stay off nonblocking FFI controls/finalizers.

Finite query IR and schema-specific Rust generation are defined sufficiently for the planned implementation gates. Build dependencies avoid source-generator ordering assumptions. AOT, actual database execution, budget bounds and semantic profiles still require the declared delivery tests.
